title: In God We Trust
tagline: Wealth can grow wings. God never does.
seo_title: In God We Trust? Money, Control and Contentment for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Trust isn't revealed in what you say but in what you lean on when pressure hits. A devotional on Proverbs 23:4-5 and Philippians 4:11-13 for men carrying what belongs to God.
verse_text: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not trust your own cleverness. Cast but a glance at riches, and they are gone, for they will surely sprout wings and fly off to the sky like an eagle.

scriptures.text: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not trust your own cleverness. Cast but a glance at riches, and they are gone, for they will surely sprout wings and fly off to the sky like an eagle.
I have learned to be content whatever the circumstances. I can do all this through him who gives me strength.

blocks.text: In God We Trust. We say it. We print it. We believe we mean it.
But trust isn't revealed in what you say. It's revealed in what you lean on when pressure hits.
Proverbs cuts straight through the illusion: riches sprout wings and fly off. We exhaust ourselves chasing something that disappears mid-grab. Not slowly. Not eventually. Suddenly.
Most men don't think they're trusting money. They think they're being responsible: providing, planning, building.

items: But underneath, there's often a quieter driver.
- If I don't secure this, I'm not safe.
- If I don't achieve this, I'm not enough.
- If I don't control this, everything falls apart.

blocks.text: So we grind. We strategize. We carry weight God never asked us to hold. And the crazy part is that it feels wise.
The lie isn't "Money is your god." That's too obvious.
The real lie is: "God helps, but you're still the source."
So we pray like God is the provider and operate like it all depends on us. That tension will wear a man out.
Then Philippians gives a completely different operating system. Paul has learned to be content in every circumstance.
He isn't talking about having more. He's talking about needing less to be okay. That's real strength. Not control, not accumulation, not insulation from risk. Contentment.
Contentment is what happens when you stop trying to be your own provider and start trusting God as your source.
You don't discover trust in your theology. You discover it in your reflexes.
When pressure hits, where do you go first? Your effort? Your plan? Your network? Your control? Or Him?
Whatever you run to first is what you actually trust.
You're not exhausted because you're doing too much. You're exhausted because you're carrying something you were never designed to carry: provision, outcome, security, identity.
That's God's lane. And every time you step into it, you feel the weight of a role you were never meant to play.
God isn't inviting you into less responsibility, but different reliance. Not passivity, but partnership. Not "stop working," but stop sourcing.
You work hard, but you don't carry the outcome. You plan wisely, but you don't worship the plan. You build faithfully, but you don't anchor your identity to what you build.

items: Where did I feel pressure to make something happen instead of trusting God to move?
When pressure hits, what do I run to first?
What am I carrying that belongs in God's lane?
show me where I've been carrying what belongs to You.
Expose the places where I've trusted my effort more than Your provision.
Teach me contentment that isn't dependent on outcomes.
Rewire my reflexes to run to You first.
I trust You as my source,
not just in what I say, but in how I live.

blocks.text: Wealth can grow wings. God never does.
